_comment: Cases for src/agent_cli/dispatch.py:evaluate(root, d). `input` is the minimal `d` dict evaluate() reads (root is supplied by the test fixture, not part of `input`); `expect` checks only `state` and `auto_resume`, the two fields evaluate()'s decision table sets. `worktree` in every case points at a path that does not exist on disk, so evaluate()'s git cross-checks (_cross_check_commits/_synthesize, gated on Path(worktree).exists()) are no-ops and the case stays pure. Each case's `note` records its nuance.

cases.name: question_no_denials_never_auto_resumes
cases.note: a worker that returns `question` used to get one free auto-resumed re-read of the plan. That is exactly the guessing the harness's top rule forbids, and it cost real money twice. A plain question always goes to the owner now; evaluate() sets no auto_resume for it.

structured_output.summary: need a decision on which pattern to follow: modal or inline
open_questions: mirror pattern A or pattern B?

cases.name: question_demoted_to_blocked_by_permission_denials
cases.note: a question raised because a command was DENIED is a harness fault, not worker hesitation. evaluate() demotes it to `blocked` (still no auto_resume — only the owner can widen a permission) instead of treating it as an ordinary question. A `pnpm --filter x lint` denial is this shape.

structured_output.summary: pnpm lint was denied; need a wider rule before I can verify anything
open_questions: can dispatch.allowed_tools be widened for pnpm --filter?

cases.name: timeout_proposes_one_auto_resume
cases.note: evaluate() always proposes auto_resume="timeout" when timed_out is true — the cap that makes this happen only once per dispatch (`d["attempt"] < d["max_attempts"]`, MAX_ATTEMPTS=2) lives in run()'s loop, not in evaluate() itself, since evaluate() is pure and never reads max_attempts. See the second timeout case below and the README for why that split is deliberate.

cases.name: timeout_on_the_last_attempt_still_proposes_resume
cases.note: Same input shape at attempt 2 of 2 (the last one MAX_ATTEMPTS allows): evaluate() still returns auto_resume="timeout". run() is what reads attempt<max_attempts and stops proposing after this one — evaluate() does not know it is the last attempt. Documented rather than asserted against run() here, since item 1 covers evaluate() in isolation; a run()-level test belongs to whichever item exercises the supervisor loop (tests/test_dispatch.py already does, e.g. its MAX_ATTEMPTS-bounded auto-resume tests).

cases.name: budget_hit_is_blocked_not_auto_resumed
cases.note: a budget hit auto-raising itself behind the owner's back happened twice in six days and once answered a real design question for them. evaluate() never sets auto_resume for a budget hit, valid return or not; it always reads `blocked`.

cases.name: max_turns_hit_is_blocked_not_auto_resumed
cases.note: `dispatch.max_turns` is the third bound on a runaway worker, beside the budget and the clock, and the only one that is not paid in full before it stops anything. The CLI reports it as the result subtype `error_max_turns`; evaluate() reads it the same way it reads a budget hit — off the envelope, never the exit code — and lands `blocked` with no auto_resume, because raising the cap or narrowing the task is the owner's call, exactly as it is for a budget hit.

cases.name: done_stays_done
cases.note: A clean, schema-valid `done` return with a matching nonce and session_id: evaluate() passes the worker's own status straight through.

structured_output.summary: added the field and its tests

cases.name: a_legacy_done_whose_reported_commands_miss_a_retired_check_stays_done
cases.note: The worker-reported required_checks gate is retired: workers no longer report commands, and the supervisor's own verification decides acceptance at finalize. A return in the earlier shape (branch, commits, files_touched, commands) is still collected, its retired fields dropped, and a regex its commands never matched no longer demotes it. `required_checks` stays on the case only to show it is ignored.

structured_output.summary: added the column and wired it up

cases.name: done_that_ran_every_required_check_stays_done
cases.note: The other direction of the same branch, so the case above cannot pass by the checks never being read: same repo, same required check, and a return whose `commands` ran it at exit 0. A required check satisfied by a non-zero exit does NOT count (`check_returns` asks for both), which is why the exit is asserted here rather than only the command text.

structured_output.summary: added the column and wired it up

cases.name: blocked_stays_blocked
cases.note: A worker that self-reports `blocked` (no timeout, no budget hit, no denials) passes straight through, same as `done` and `question` do.

structured_output.summary: the migration needs a column that does not exist yet

cases.name: no_result_at_all_is_failed
cases.note: A transport failure with no envelope: the worker produced no result and the exit code is non-zero (a budget hit exits 1, not 2, so exit code alone was never a usable signal either — this case is the true 'nothing came back' failure, not a budget hit).
